## Prodigi vs Gelato for Framed Prints and Canvas (UK, EU, US)
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/prodigi-vs-gelato/
Prodigi and Gelato compared for wall art sellers in the UK, EU and US: framed canvas gap and depth, frames, mounts, where each prints, samples and mockups.

Short answer: Prodigi suits sellers who want detailed specs and more frame choice: a floater framed canvas with a 5 mm gap in six colours, box and classic frames, and optional mounts in three colours, fulfilled from the UK, EU, US and Australia. Gelato suits sellers who want a wide local network (32 countries) and a simpler range: framed canvas in three colours with a 12 mm gap, and framed posters in wood or metal. Check the regional differences, then order a sample.

Q: Is Prodigi or Gelato better for framed prints?
A: Prodigi lists more frame types and colours and optional mounts in three colours. Gelato offers framed posters in wood and metal colours through a 32-country network. Choose by the frame you want and where your buyers are, then order a sample.
Q: Which has the wider gap on framed canvas?
A: Gelato states a 12 mm gap between canvas and frame. Prodigi's floater framed canvas has a 5 mm gap.
Q: Does Gelato offer mats or mounts?
A: The Gelato help pages we checked don't mention mats (checked 2026-10-29). Prodigi offers optional mounts in snow white, off-white and black on its classic and box frames.
Q: Where do Prodigi and Gelato print?
A: Prodigi has its own facilities in the UK, EU and USA plus partners in over 10 countries, and fulfils wall art from the UK, EU, US and Australia. Gelato produces locally in 32 countries and says you can't choose the production country.
Q: Which offers bigger framed canvas sizes?
A: Prodigi's framed canvas runs from 4×6 in to 55×55 in. Gelato's comes in 13 sizes from 8×10 in to 24×36 in.
Q: Do Prodigi and Gelato give sample discounts?
A: Prodigi offers 50% off a first sample order. Gelato offers new sellers 30% off the product cost of a first sample order within 48 hours of sign-up, up to 50€ off.

## Replace Printify and Printful Mockups on Etsy and Shopify
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/replace-printify-and-printful-mockups/
Step by step: swap Printify and Printful default mockups for your own room photos on Etsy and Shopify, and the settings that keep every product in sync.

Short answer: Both Printify and Printful let you use your own photos in Etsy or Shopify; republishing over them and editing variants or SKUs are the real risks. With Printify, either upload your images in its Mockup Library, or add them on Etsy or Shopify and untick Mockups every time you republish. Printful can't take your files, so add them in your store, keep a photo slot free on Etsy, and check the listing after any mockup refresh. Make every other change inside Printify or Printful.

Q: Will replacing Printify mockups break the sync?
A: Not by itself. Printify's selective publishing keeps manually uploaded mockups as long as you leave Mockups unticked when you republish. Changing variants, IDs or SKUs in your store is what causes sync problems.
Q: How do I stop Printify overwriting my Etsy photos?
A: Publish updates with only the changed details ticked and Mockups unticked. Printify says publishing its mockups replaces your Etsy mockups, including videos.
Q: Can I upload my own mockups to Printful?
A: No. Printful says it isn't possible to upload mockup images to Printful. Add them directly to your Etsy or Shopify listing.
Q: Why are my old Printful mockups still on the listing?
A: Printful says some integrations add new mockups without removing the old ones. Delete the old images in your store, then put your room photo back in first place.
Q: How many photos can I add to a Shopify product?
A: Shopify allows up to 250 images, 3D models or videos per product, with one image per variant.
Q: Does WallMock upload photos to Printify, Printful or Etsy?
A: No. WallMock makes the room photos; you upload them to your provider's mockup library or your store yourself.

## Room Mockup vs White Background vs Close-Up for Wall Art
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/room-mockup-vs-white-background/
Room mockup vs white background vs close-up for wall art listings: what each photo answers, which goes first, and the unedited photo Etsy asks for on most listings.

Short answer: Wall art listings need all three, each for a different job. Lead with a room scene, because it shows style and scale at thumbnail size. Use one plain or white background image for the full, uncropped artwork, and a close-up for the frame, mat or canvas edge. On Etsy, add an unedited photo of a real sample too: most listings need one, with an exception for authorised print-on-demand mockups.

Q: Do room mockups sell better than white background photos?
A: No platform publishes figures comparing them. Room scenes usually lead because they show style and scale at thumbnail size; a white-background image does a different job, showing the whole artwork.
Q: Should my first Etsy photo be on a white background?
A: Usually not for wall art. A room scene reads better in search. Etsy asks that the first photo is the clearest, most realistic view of what the buyer receives, so show the product you actually ship.
Q: Do I need a real photo if I use mockups on Etsy?
A: Most Etsy listings need at least one unedited photo of the actual item. Print-on-demand items can use an authorised stock mockup instead; read Etsy's listing image requirements for your product.
Q: What should a wall art close-up show?
A: The detail buyers can't see from across a room: the floating gap and frame on a framed canvas, the edge and depth on a stretched canvas, or the mat and frame corner on a framed print.

## Room Styles and Wall Colours That Make Wall Art Sell
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/room-styles-and-wall-colours-for-wall-art-mockups/
When to use neutral, tinted and bold rooms; which interior styles suit which art; and how to match wall colours to your artwork's palette.

Short answer: Use a warm neutral room (white, cream, greige or sand) for the first photo, where the art must stand out in search. Add soft tinted rooms such as sage or blush for gentle contrast, and one bold room in deep green, navy or terracotta as an alternative. Match the interior style to your buyer, and let the wall contrast with the artwork's main colours.

Q: What wall colour makes art stand out most?
A: Contrast: light art on a deep wall, or dark art on a light wall. For a first listing image, a warm neutral wall is the safest choice.
Q: Should my mockup rooms match my brand?
A: A consistent palette of rooms makes a shop look coherent. Keep a few signature rooms and rotate alternatives around them.
Q: Which room style suits which art?
A: Scandinavian and Japandi rooms suit minimal line art, photography and abstracts; boho and Mediterranean rooms suit warm, textured and botanical work; classic rooms with mouldings suit traditional paintings and gold frames; nurseries suit playful prints and soft colours.

## How to Sell Photography Prints as Canvas and Framed Prints
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/sell-photography-prints-canvas-and-framed/
Turn your photographs into canvas and framed print listings: print sizes from camera files, which product suits which photo, and room mockups that sell.

Short answer: Choose the product per photo: framed prints with a mat for fine detail, black-and-white and smaller sizes; canvas or floating-frame canvas for big, soft, painterly scenes. Check the file: a 24-megapixel image (6000 × 4000 px) prints 20 × 13.3 inches at 300 DPI. Crop to standard ratios, order a sample, then list each photo with a room hero, a close-up of the frame and a scale shot, through a print-on-demand partner on Etsy or Shopify.

Q: How do I sell my photography as prints?
A: Choose a product for each photo, check the file is big enough, crop to standard ratios, order a sample, and list through a print-on-demand partner on Etsy or Shopify with room mockups and a sample photo.
Q: How big can I print a 24-megapixel photo?
A: A 6000 × 4000 px file prints 20 × 13.3 inches at 300 DPI, or about 40 × 26.7 inches at 150 DPI, before any cropping.
Q: Should I sell photos as canvas or framed prints?
A: Framed prints with a mat suit fine detail, black and white and smaller sizes. Canvas suits large, soft, painterly scenes. Many photographers offer both.
Q: Which ratio should I crop photos to?
A: Camera files are usually 3:2, which prints at 4×6, 8×12, 12×18, 16×24, 20×30 and 24×36 inches without cropping. Sizes like 8×10 and 16×20 need a crop.
Q: Can I use mockups for photography listings on Etsy?
A: Yes, if they accurately show what the buyer receives. Most items also need an unedited photo; print-on-demand items may use an authorised stock mockup instead.

## How to Sell Wall Art on Shopify with Print on Demand
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/sell-wall-art-on-shopify/
Set up framed canvas, framed prints and posters on Shopify with a print-on-demand app: products, variants, image sizes and the photos each product page needs.

Short answer: Install a print-on-demand app such as Printify, Printful or Gelato from the Shopify App Store, create each artwork as a product in the provider's app, and publish it to your store. Shopify allows up to three options and 2,048 variants per product, so size × frame colour fits in one product. Then replace generic provider images with room photos that match each frame and size, around 2048 × 2048 px.

Q: Can you sell wall art on Shopify with print on demand?
A: Yes. Install a print-on-demand app from the Shopify App Store, create your artwork as products in it, and publish them to your store. The provider prints and ships each order.
Q: Which print-on-demand apps work with Shopify for wall art?
A: Printify, Printful and Gelato all have apps in the Shopify App Store and list wall art among their products. Compare their frames, sizes and print locations before you choose.
Q: How many variants can a Shopify product have?
A: Shopify's help centre says up to 2,048 variants and up to three options per product. Size, frame colour and mat are typical options for wall art.
Q: What size should Shopify product images be?
A: Shopify says square images of 2048 × 2048 px usually display best. Images can be up to 5000 × 5000 px or 25 megapixels, and must be under 20 MB.
Q: Should framed and unframed versions be one product or two?
A: Either works. Separate products keep photos and prices clear; one product with a product-type option means fewer pages, as long as each variant has its own matching photo.
Q: Does WallMock upload images to Shopify?
A: No. WallMock makes the room images; you download them and add them to your Shopify products or variants.

## Selling AI or Midjourney Art Prints on Etsy: Disclosure
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/selling-ai-art-prints-on-etsy/
What to check before selling AI-assisted wall art on Etsy: disclosure, the tool's terms, originality, print quality and honest mockups.

Short answer: Etsy's creativity standards allow items designed with AI tools from your own prompts, but you must disclose AI use in the listing. Before you list, check your image generator's terms for your plan, avoid copying named artists, characters or photos, clean and upscale the file for each print ratio, and use mockups that show your exact file at its true ratio. This is a checklist, not legal advice.

Q: Can you sell AI-generated art on Etsy?
A: Etsy's creativity standards allow items designed with AI tools from your own prompts, provided you disclose it. Check Etsy's current policy before listing.
Q: Do I need to say my art is AI-generated?
A: On Etsy, yes: sellers are asked to disclose AI use in the listing description. It is also the honest thing to tell buyers.
Q: Can I use mockups made with AI?
A: Mockup rooms can be digitally staged, but the artwork shown must be your actual file at its true proportions, so buyers see what they will receive.

## Shopify Wall Art Product Images: Variant Photos That Match
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/shopify-wall-art-product-images/
Shopify product images for wall art: options for size and frame, one image per variant, the gallery order, image sizes, and fixing photos a print-on-demand sync broke.

Short answer: Give each frame colour variant its own image from the product's media, made in the same room so only the frame changes, then group the extra photos for that colour next to it in the gallery. Shopify allows one assigned image per variant, up to 250 media items per product and up to 2,048 variants. Square images around 2048 × 2048 px usually display best. After a print-on-demand sync, check every variant still points to the right photo.

Q: Can a Shopify variant have more than one image?
A: No. Shopify allows one assigned image per variant, chosen from the product's media. Put the other photos for that variant next to it in the gallery so buyers see them together.
Q: What size should Shopify product images be?
A: Shopify says 2048 × 2048 px usually displays best for square product images. Images can be up to 5000 × 5000 px or 25 megapixels, and must be under 20 MB.
Q: How many variants can a Shopify product have?
A: Up to 2,048 variants and 3 options. Shopify warns that some themes, apps and sales channels might not support more than 100 variants.
Q: Why did my Printify or Printful sync replace my Shopify photos?
A: Publishing the app's mockups again can replace the images on the product. Use the app's publish settings to leave images alone, and keep your own copies so you can reassign them quickly.
Q: Does WallMock upload images to Shopify?

## Smartmockups Alternatives for Wall Art Sellers
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/smartmockups-alternatives-for-wall-art/
Smartmockups.com closed on 27 September 2024. What happened to your mockups, what moved into Canva, and four kinds of alternative for wall art listings.

Short answer: Smartmockups.com closed on 27 September 2024, according to Canva's help centre, and the old address now redirects to Canva's mockups page. Mockups you exported before stay royalty-free for personal or commercial projects. For wall art, the alternatives are Canva's own mockups, Photoshop PSD templates, your print provider's mockup generator, or a wall art mockup generator built for framed canvas, framed prints and whole collections.

Q: Is Smartmockups still available?
A: No. Canva's help centre says Smartmockups.com closed on 27 September 2024, and the old address now redirects to Canva's mockups page.
Q: Can I still use mockups I made in Smartmockups?
A: Yes. Canva's help centre says previously exported Smartmockups mockups are royalty-free and can still be used in personal or commercial projects. You may not resell the empty mockups or use them as stock photos.
Q: What replaced Smartmockups?
A: Canva says the Smartmockups team is now building mockup tools inside Canva. Other options are Photoshop PSD templates, print provider mockups and wall art mockup generators.
Q: What is a good Smartmockups alternative for wall art?

Q: Does WallMock make mockups for T-shirts or mugs?
A: No. WallMock only makes wall art mockups: framed canvas, stretched canvas, and framed prints or posters (wood frame or aluminum framed print) with or without a mat, and metal prints.

## Upscale AI Art for Print: Large Canvas and Framed Prints
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/upscale-ai-art-for-print/
How many pixels a large canvas or framed print needs, how to upscale AI art in steps, and how to spot the artefacts upscalers add before you send a file to print.

Short answer: Work out the pixels first: print inches × 300 for prints seen up close, or × 150 for large canvas seen from across a room, the lowest Prodigi and Gelato suggest. Fix defects and crop to the final ratio at the original size, then upscale in one or two 2× to 4× steps with a gentle setting. Inspect at 100% for invented texture, smeared lettering and halos, and keep a lossless master.

Q: What DPI do I need for a canvas print?
A: Aim for 300 DPI at the final size. Prodigi says 150 may be enough for work without fine detail, and Gelato advises against going under 150 DPI.
Q: How many pixels do I need for a 24 × 36 inch print?
A: 7,200 × 10,800 pixels at 300 DPI, or 3,600 × 5,400 at 150 DPI.
Q: Is it OK to upscale AI art for print?
A: Yes, if you check the result at 100% for artefacts and fix defects before enlarging. The artwork also has to be yours to sell, and Etsy asks you to disclose AI-made items.
Q: Should I upscale 2× or 4×?
A: Use the smallest step that reaches the pixels you need. One 4× step from a clean original is usually better than several stacked passes.
Q: Why does my upscaled art look plastic?
A: The upscaler's strength or detail setting is too high, so it smooths and repaints. Use the art mode, lower the strength, or blend in a plain enlargement.
Q: Does WallMock upscale my art?
A: No. WallMock places your file as it is: it is never redrawn, repainted or upscaled by AI. Upscale your print master yourself, then make mockups from it.

## Wall Art Listing Mistakes Behind Returns and Bad Reviews
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/wall-art-listing-mistakes/
The wall art listing mistakes behind returns and 'not as described' cases: frame not included, wrong size, colour shift, wrong finish, cropped art, and the fixes.

Short answer: Many wall art returns start with a listing that promised something different: a frame that isn't included, a size that looks bigger in the mockup, colours brighter than the print, a different frame finish, or art cropped to fit a size. On Etsy, an item that differs from its photos or description can become a case where the seller refunds the item, the original shipping and the return shipping. Make every photo and line match what arrives.

Q: What counts as 'not as described' on Etsy?
A: Etsy's help page says it can include an item whose colour, design or model differs from what the listing description and photos showed, the wrong quantity, or a misrepresented condition.
Q: Who pays for returns when wall art is not as described?
A: If Etsy decides the item doesn't match the listing, the seller must refund the item, the original shipping and the return shipping.
Q: Do I have to accept returns on Etsy?
A: Etsy says sellers aren't required to accept returns, exchanges or refunds unless their return policy says so. An item that doesn't match its listing can still lead to a case and a refund.
Q: How do I stop 'it's smaller than I expected' reviews?
A: Show one realistic size in every room photo, add a size guide with every size labelled in inches and centimetres, and state the outer size for framed items.
Q: Are mockups the cause of returns?
A: Not by themselves. Returns come from mockups that show a different product, size, finish or colour from what arrives. A mockup that matches the item is fine.

## Wall Art Mockup Cost: Etsy Packs, Subscriptions or Per Room
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/wall-art-mockup-costs/
Work out the real cost per listing photo for mockup packs, subscriptions and per-room pricing, including your time, with a worked example and WallMock's prices.

Short answer: Compare cost per finished listing image, not the price tag. A one-off pack costs its price divided by the images you'll actually make from it, plus your editing time. A subscription costs its monthly price divided by the images you make that month. Per-room or per-image pricing is cheap for a few images and grows with every one. For most shops, time is the biggest cost. WallMock costs $5 a month for 200 images, or $12 for unlimited clean 4K (4096 px) images.

Q: How much do wall art mockups cost?
A: It depends on the model and your time. On one Etsy search we ran on 29 October 2026, half the framed canvas mockup bundles cost about 5 to 15 US dollars. Subscriptions charge monthly. Compare cost per image, including your time.
Q: Are free mockups really free?
A: They cost nothing up front, but you still pay in time, and some need attribution or limit commercial use. Other shops may use the same scenes.
Q: Is a mockup subscription worth it?
A: If you list new designs regularly, usually yes, because the setup is reused and the time per image drops. For a few designs a year, a pack can be cheaper.
Q: How much does WallMock cost?
A: Lite is $5 a month for 200 clean 4K images. Pro ($12) and Studio ($24) include unlimited clean 4K (4096 px) images. Fair use: up to 150 new rooms a day and 400 in 30 days, and up to 300 images a day made on WallMock's server (600 on Studio). Previews are free and watermarked.
Q: What counts as one image in WallMock?
A: One clean, full-size download of one artwork in one room. Watermarked previews don't count.
Q: Can I keep using WallMock images after I cancel?
A: Yes. WallMock's terms say the licence to the room scenes and frames in your finished images continues after you cancel or close your account.

## Wall Art Mockups for Pinterest and Instagram: 2:3 and 4:5
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/wall-art-mockups-for-pinterest-and-instagram/
Crop wall art mockups for Pinterest (2:3, 1000 × 1500 px) and Instagram (4:5, up to 1440 px wide) without cutting the frame, plus titles, links and video sizes.

Short answer: Pinterest recommends 2:3 images at 1000 × 1500 px, so crop your wall art mockup to a tall 2:3 with the whole frame inside. For an Instagram feed post, use 4:5 portrait: Meta's Instagram publishing documentation accepts 4:5 to 1.91:1 and scales images down to 1440 px wide, so 1440 × 1800 px is the largest 4:5. Crop from your full-size export, keep space around the art, and link each pin to the listing.

Q: What size should a Pinterest pin be for wall art?
A: Pinterest recommends a 2:3 image at 1000 × 1500 px. Crop the room mockup so the whole frame sits inside with wall around it.
Q: What size should an Instagram post of wall art be?
A: Use 4:5 portrait. Meta's Instagram publishing documentation accepts 4:5 to 1.91:1 and scales images down to 1440 px wide, so 1440 × 1800 px is the largest 4:5.
Q: Can I use the same mockup for Pinterest and Instagram?
A: Yes. Crop one full-size room image twice: a 2:3 crop for Pinterest and a 4:5 crop for Instagram, keeping the art centred in both.
Q: Should Pinterest pins link to Etsy?
A: Link each pin to the exact listing. On Etsy, a Share & Save trackable link earns a 4% refund on eligible orders placed within 30 days of a click.
Q: What about video pins?
A: Pinterest recommends 9:16 at 1080 × 1920 px for video, with space left at the top and bottom for the player controls.

## Wall Art Placement in Mockups: Size, Balance, Usable Wall
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/wall-art-placement/
Place art convincingly in a mockup: find the usable wall, choose the visual anchor, size it without crowding, respect its ratio, and check perspective and light.

Short answer: Find the uninterrupted wall that can hold the whole framed piece, then centre the art on its visual anchor, such as a sofa, sideboard or chair, rather than on the photo. Start generous, check clearance from lamps, doors and ceilings, keep the artwork's own ratio, match perspective and light on angled walls, and check the result at thumbnail size.

Q: Where should art go in a mockup?
A: On the uninterrupted wall that can hold the whole framed piece, centred on its visual anchor, such as the sofa, sideboard or chair below it.
Q: Should art be centred in the photo?
A: Not necessarily. The centre of the photo is often not the centre of the usable wall; centre the art on the furniture or wall area it belongs to.
Q: Can a mockup show exact hanging dimensions?
A: Only if the scene has reliable scale information. Room staging is a visual presentation, not a calibrated measuring tool.

## Wall Art Selling Calendar: Seasonal Dates by Country
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/wall-art-selling-calendar/
When buyers shop for wall art through the year, in the US, UK, Europe, Canada, Australia and India, and how far ahead to list and update your mockups.

Short answer: List new collections and refresh mockups six to eight weeks before each peak: by early December for the new year, late December for Valentine's Day, mid-January for Mothering Sunday in the UK, mid-March for Mother's Day in May, late April for Father's Day in June, and October for Christmas. For many shops, October to December is the biggest season of the year.

Q: When should I list Christmas wall art?
A: By October, so listings have time to appear in search before the December peak. Start on cosy seasonal mockups in September.
Q: Is Mother's Day on the same date everywhere?
A: No. It is in March in the UK and Ireland, the first Sunday of May in Spain and Portugal, the second Sunday of May in the US, Canada, Australia, India and much of Europe, and late May or early June in France.
Q: How far ahead should I list seasonal wall art?
A: About six to eight weeks before the peak, then refresh the hero image as the date approaches.

## Wall Art Size Guide Image: Show Buyers How Big Each Size Is
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/wall-art-size-guide-image/
How to make a wall art size guide image for Etsy or Shopify: which sizes to show, inches and centimetres, frame outer sizes, a scale photo, and what to avoid.

Short answer: A wall art size guide image shows every size you sell side by side, drawn in proportion to each other, each labelled in inches and centimetres. Show only sizes in your artwork's ratio, say whether the numbers are the artwork or the framed outside size, and pair it with one room photo above familiar furniture for real-life scale. Make it the same shape as your first photo, and repeat the sizes in the description.

Q: What should a wall art size chart include?
A: Every size you sell, drawn in proportion to each other, labelled in inches and centimetres, with a note saying whether the numbers are the artwork or the framed outer size.
Q: Should I show sizes in inches or centimetres?
A: Both. Lead with the unit most of your buyers use and put the other beside it, for example 16 × 24 in (about 41 × 61 cm).
Q: Do frame sizes include the frame?
A: Say which. A floating frame or a mat adds to the outer size, so a 16 × 24 in canvas in a floating frame measures more than 16 × 24 in outside.
Q: Is a room mockup enough to show size?
A: No. A room photo gives a feel for scale, but buyers can't measure from it. Add a size guide image with the exact sizes, and list them in the description.
Q: Is WallMock's size guide image true to scale?
A: It draws the sizes in proportion to each other, in centimetres and inches: the sizes you entered, or example sizes if you entered none. It compares the sizes with each other; it is not your art measured on a wall. Check the sizes against what you sell before publishing.

## Wall Art Trends 2027 and the Rooms to Show Them In
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/wall-art-trends-2027/
Six wall art directions to watch for 2027, with Etsy's own search data where it exists, clearly labelled observations, and the room styles that suit each.

Short answer: No one can measure 2027 yet, so treat every trend list as observation. The firmest data is Etsy's: searches for wall art decor rose 110% and gallery prints 80% in the three months to 10 February 2026, year on year, among US signed-in shoppers. The directions we see carrying into 2027 are gallery-wall sets, nostalgic art, deep wall colours, warm natural materials, big statement pieces and quiet photography. Show each in a room that suits it.

Q: What are the wall art trends for 2027?
A: No one has 2027 data yet. Etsy's latest trend post shows strong search growth for wall art decor and gallery prints. We also see gallery-wall sets, nostalgic art, deep wall colours, warm natural materials, statement pieces and quiet photography carrying on.
Q: Is gallery wall art still popular?
A: Etsy reported searches for gallery prints up 80% and wall art decor up 110% in the three months to 10 February 2026, compared with a year earlier, among US signed-in users.
Q: Are dark walls good for wall art mockups?
A: Yes, as an alternative image. Pale art, black-and-white photos and gold frames stand out on deep walls. Keep a neutral room for the first photo.
Q: Should I change my art to follow trends?
A: Usually not. Change the rooms and frames you show it in, which is cheaper and keeps your style consistent.
Q: Where does Etsy publish trend data?
A: Etsy's trend expert posts seasonal trend reports in the Etsy Community, in the Etsy Success forum. Check there for newer reports.

## What DPI Does a Canvas Print Need? Pixels by Size
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/what-dpi-for-canvas-prints/
Canvas print DPI explained: what Gelato, Prodigi, Printful and Printify recommend, the pixels each canvas size needs at 150 to 300 DPI, and the extra for wrapped edges.

Short answer: Aim for 300 DPI at the final canvas size: Gelato, Prodigi, Printful and Printify each name 300 DPI as ideal (checked 2026-10-29), and Gelato says files under 150 DPI are not recommended. Pixels = inches × DPI: a 16×20 in canvas needs 4,800 × 6,000 px at 300 DPI, or 2,400 × 3,000 at 150. For an image-wrapped canvas, add the depth to every side first: a 16×20 in canvas 1.5 in deep needs 19×23 in of picture.

Q: Is 150 DPI OK for a canvas print?
A: For large canvases seen from across a room, usually yes; it is the floor Gelato sets. Providers recommend 300 DPI, so aim higher for small canvases viewed up close.
Q: What resolution do I need for a 24×36 canvas?
A: 7,200 × 10,800 px for 300 DPI, or 3,600 × 5,400 px for 150 DPI. Add the wrap if the image continues round the sides: 27×39 in for a 1.5 in deep canvas.
Q: Do I need 300 DPI for a 40×60 canvas?
A: That would be 12,000 × 18,000 px, which few files reach. Many sellers print large canvas at 150 to 200 DPI, which is 6,000 × 9,000 to 8,000 × 12,000 px.
Q: Does mirror wrap need a bigger file?
A: No. With mirror wrap or plain sides, the provider fills the sides, so the file only needs to cover the front. Image wrap needs the extra.
Q: How do I change the DPI of my image?
A: Changing the DPI setting alone does nothing. Print quality depends on pixel width and height, so you need a bigger file or a smaller print.
Q: Will WallMock upscale my art?
A: WallMock places your file as it is: it is never redrawn, repainted or upscaled by AI.

## What Is a Floater Frame? Floating Frame vs Gallery Wrap
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/what-is-a-floater-frame/
A floater frame holds a canvas from behind with a small gap and no glass. How it differs from a standard frame, a shadow box, a gallery wrap and a matted frame.

Short answer: A floater frame, or floating frame, is an open frame that holds a stretched canvas from behind, with a small gap between the canvas edge and the frame on every side. Nothing covers the front of the canvas, and there is no glass and no mat, so the canvas seems to float inside the frame. The providers we checked use gaps of 5 to 12 mm. A standard frame overlaps the art's edges, usually behind glass; a gallery wrap has no frame at all.

Q: Do floating frames have glass?
A: No. A floating frame for canvas is open at the front, with no glass, acrylic or mat. The canvas surface shows directly.
Q: How big is the gap in a floating frame?
A: Usually a few millimetres to about a centimetre. Prodigi lists 5 mm and Gelato 12 mm for their framed canvas (checked 2026-10-29).
Q: Can you put a paper print in a floating frame?
A: Not in a canvas floater. A paper print needs glass and a backing, so it goes in a standard frame, or is float-mounted in a deeper frame behind glass.
Q: Is a floating frame the same as a shadow box?
A: No. A shadow box is a deep frame with glass and space for objects. A floating frame has no glass and holds a stretched canvas.
Q: Is a framed canvas always a floating frame?
A: In print on demand it usually is. Prodigi calls its framed canvas a floater frame and Printful says its frame gives a floating effect, but check your own provider's page.
Q: What is the difference between a gallery wrap and a floater frame?
A: A gallery wrap is a stretched canvas hung on its own, with its sides finished. A floater frame is an open frame added around such a canvas, with a gap between them.

## How High to Hang Art Over a Sofa, Bed or Sideboard
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/what-size-art-over-sofa-and-bed/
How high to hang art above a sofa, bed, sideboard or open wall, how wide it should be, and the print sizes that fit common furniture widths. With tables.

Short answer: Hang the bottom of the frame about 6–10 inches (15–25 cm) above a sofa back, 8–12 inches (20–30 cm) above a headboard and 4–8 inches (10–20 cm) above a sideboard. On an open wall, put the centre of the art about 57–60 inches (145–152 cm) from the floor. For width, aim for about two thirds to three quarters of the furniture below, measuring a pair or trio as one group.

Q: How high should art hang above a sofa?
A: The bottom of the frame about 6–10 inches (15–25 cm) above the sofa back.
Q: How high should art hang above a bed?
A: About 8–12 inches (20–30 cm) above the headboard, so nobody hits the frame when sitting up. Measure the headboard rather than the mattress if it is wider.
Q: How big should art be over a couch?
A: About two thirds to three quarters of the couch's width, including the frame. For an 84-inch sofa that is roughly 56–63 inches of art, or a group of pieces that wide.
Q: What size art goes above a queen bed?
A: About 40–45 inches (100–115 cm) wide, such as a 30×40 landscape, a 14×42 panorama or a pair of 16×20 landscapes.

## Why Wall Art Mockups Look Fake: Fixes for Realistic Mockups
URL: https://wallmock.com/guides/why-wall-art-mockups-look-fake/
Five things make a wall art mockup look fake: perspective, scale, light, shadow and colour. Simple checks with a ruler and a colour picker fix each one.

Short answer: Wall art mockups look fake when the art doesn't obey the room: its edges don't follow the wall's lines, its size doesn't suit the furniture, the light on it doesn't match the wall, its shadow is missing or falls the wrong way, or its whites are a different colour from the room's light. You can measure each one with a ruler tool and a colour picker. Fix the room and the placement, never the artwork's own colours.

Q: Why do my wall art mockups look fake?
A: Usually one of five things: perspective that doesn't follow the wall, a size that doesn't suit the furniture, light that doesn't match the wall, a missing or wrong-way shadow, or art whites that are a different colour from the room's light.
Q: How big should the art look in a mockup?
A: For a single piece or a group above furniture, about two thirds to three quarters of the furniture's width. Measure both in pixels and divide.
Q: Should I change my art's colours to match the room?
A: No. Etsy requires photos to show the item's true colour. Choose a room with neutral, even light instead of tinting the artwork.
Q: Does a framed canvas mockup need a shadow?
A: Yes. A floating-frame canvas stands off the wall, so it casts a soft shadow, and its gap shows as a thin dark line inside the frame. No shadow makes it look pasted on.
Q: How do I check a mockup's perspective?
A: Draw lines along the frame's edges and along nearby room edges. In a straight-on room they should be parallel. In an angled room they should meet at the same vanishing point.

16 free browser tools for wall art and print-on-demand sellers: Etsy fees, print sizes and DPI, size charts, printable packs, triptych splits, frames and gallery walls.

## Art Color Palette Generator: Extract Colors from Artwork
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/art-color-palette/
Free art color palette generator: extract the six main colours from your artwork or painting, with HEX and RGB codes and each colour's share. Nothing is uploaded.

Short answer: choose an image of your artwork and the generator finds its six main colours, with HEX and RGB codes to copy and the share of the image each one covers. It runs in your browser, and the same image always gives the same palette. Use the colours for shop branding and listing graphics, and see which frame finishes stand out most against the art.

Q: How do I get the colour codes from a painting?
A: Photograph or scan the painting straight on in even light, crop it to the artwork, then choose the file above. Each colour shows its HEX code (such as #C83C32) and RGB values, with a button to copy them.
Q: What is the difference between HEX and RGB?
A: They are two ways of writing the same colour. RGB gives the red, green and blue amounts from 0 to 255; HEX writes the same three numbers in base 16 after a #. Web pages and most design apps accept either.
Q: Will the same image always give the same palette?
A: Yes. The method has no random step, so the same file gives the same six colours and shares every time. A different photo or crop of the same painting can shift the colours slightly.
Q: Why are there sometimes fewer than six colours?
A: Only when the image has fewer than six distinct colours, such as flat graphic art. The generator never invents a colour that is not in the image.
Q: How does the frame suggestion work?
A: It compares how light or dark the artwork is overall with each of WallMock's seven frame finishes, using the contrast ratio from web accessibility guidelines. A high ratio means the frame stands out; a low one means it blends in. It ignores hue, style and the room, so treat it as a starting point.
Q: Is my image uploaded?
A: No. The image is read and measured in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere.

## What Size Art Over a Sofa or Bed? Free Art Size Calculator
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/art-size-over-sofa/
Free art size calculator: enter your sofa, bed or sideboard width to get the art width, the standard sizes that fit and how high to hang it. Inches or cm.

Short answer: art over a sofa usually looks balanced at about two-thirds to three-quarters of the sofa's width, frame included: 56 to 63 inches over an 84 inch sofa, such as a 40 × 60 landscape. Hang the bottom of the frame 6 to 10 inches above the sofa back. Enter your furniture below for the sizes that fit.

Q: What size art goes over an 84 inch sofa?
A: About 56 to 63 inches wide, frame included: two-thirds to three-quarters of the sofa. A 40 × 60 inch landscape hung wide (60 in), a 20 × 60 inch panorama, or a trio of 18 × 24 inch portraits with 3 inch gaps (60 in) all fit.
Q: What size art goes over a queen bed?
A: A US queen headboard is about 60 inches wide, so aim for 40 to 45 inches: a 30 × 40 inch landscape, a 14 × 42 inch panorama, or a pair of 20 × 30 inch portraits with a 3 inch gap (43 in). Measure the headboard if it is wider than the mattress.
Q: Does the frame count in the width?
A: Yes. The two-thirds guideline is about what you see on the wall, so measure the outside of the frame. For a pair or trio, measure the whole group, gaps included.
Q: How high should art hang over a sofa?
A: Hang the bottom of the frame about 6 to 10 inches (15 to 25 cm) above the sofa back, 8 to 12 inches (20 to 30 cm) above a headboard and 4 to 8 inches (10 to 20 cm) above a sideboard. The calculator shows the gap for the furniture you choose.
Q: Can art be wider than three-quarters of the sofa?
A: Yes. These are common interior guidelines, not rules, and a bold oversized piece can work. Art wider than the sofa itself usually looks crowded, so the calculator lists sizes up to 80% and labels the ones outside two-thirds to three-quarters.

## Aspect Ratio Calculator for Prints: Pixels, Inches, cm
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/aspect-ratio-calculator/
Free aspect ratio calculator for wall art: enter pixels, inches or cm to get the exact ratio, the nearest standard print ratio and the print sizes in that family.

Short answer: enter a width and a height in pixels, inches or centimetres. The calculator gives the exact ratio (4000 × 6000 px is 2:3), the decimal, the nearest standard print ratio and how far off it is, and the print sizes in that family, such as 8 × 12, 12 × 18 and 24 × 36 in for 2:3. It also finds a same-ratio size for any width.

Q: How do I find the aspect ratio of an image?
A: Divide the width and height by their greatest common divisor: 4000 × 6000 px becomes 2:3. The calculator does it for you and also names the nearest standard print ratio when the numbers don't divide neatly.
Q: What aspect ratio is 8 × 10?
A: 8 × 10 is 4:5, the same shape as 16 × 20 and 24 × 30. It is not the same shape as 8 × 12 (2:3).
Q: What aspect ratio is A4?
A: All ISO A sizes share one shape, 1:√2, about 1:1.414. A4 at 300 DPI is 2480 × 3508 px.
Q: Does the unit matter?
A: No. The ratio of 4000 × 6000 px is the same as 12 × 18 in or 30.48 × 45.72 cm. Choose the unit only so the same-ratio size comes out in it.

## Crop Image for Print: 8 × 10, 2:3, A4 at Full Resolution
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/crop-to-print-size/
Free tool to crop an image for print: 8 × 10, 2:3, 3:4, 5:7, 11 × 14, square, A4 or 3:1 panorama, at full resolution, with the print size at 300 DPI. Nothing uploaded.

Short answer: choose a print shape, such as 4:5 for 8 × 10 or 2:3 for 12 × 18, and the cropper draws the largest box of that shape your image holds. Move or resize it, see how big it prints at 300 DPI, and download the crop at full resolution as a PNG or JPEG. A 4000 × 6000 px file cropped to 8 × 10 keeps 4000 × 5000 px. Your image never leaves your device.

Q: How do I crop an image to 8 × 10?
A: Choose the 4:5 shape: 8 × 10 is 4:5, like 4 × 5, 16 × 20 and 24 × 30. The cropper draws the largest 4:5 box your image holds; move it to frame the art, then download. A 2:3 file loses about 16.7% of its height to an 8 × 10 crop.
Q: Does cropping lower the quality of my art?
A: No. The crop keeps the original pixels at full resolution; it only removes the edges. It does leave fewer pixels, so the largest size you can print sharply gets smaller. PNG keeps every pixel exactly; JPEG at quality 95 makes a smaller file with very slight compression.
Q: What shape is an A4 print?
A: All A sizes share one shape, 1:√2 (about 1:1.414). One ISO A crop prints at A5, A4, A3, A2, A1 or A0; only the size changes.
Q: Why is 8 × 10 a different shape from 8 × 12?
A: 8 × 10 is 4:5 and 8 × 12 is 2:3. Most cameras and many artworks are 2:3, so they fit 8 × 12, 12 × 18 and 24 × 36 without cropping, but lose part of the image at 8 × 10 or 16 × 20.
Q: Is my image uploaded?
A: No. The image is opened and cropped in your browser, and the download is made on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere.
Q: Can I crop a 3:1 panorama?
A: Yes. Choose the 1:3 panorama shape and Landscape for a 3:1 crop, such as 12 × 36 or 20 × 60 inches; Portrait gives a tall 1:3 crop.

## Etsy Fee Calculator: Fees, Profit and Break-Even Price
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/etsy-fee-calculator/
Free Etsy fee calculator for wall art and print-on-demand sellers: every Etsy fee, your profit, margin and break-even price, with Etsy's rates for 64 countries.

Short answer: Etsy takes USD 0.20 per listing, 6.5% of the item price plus shipping, and payment processing (3% + USD 0.25 in the US, 4% + GBP 0.20 in the UK). A sale from an Offsite Ad adds 12% or 15%. On a USD 45 print with free shipping the fees are USD 4.73. Enter your price and your provider's costs below to see your profit and break-even price.

Q: How much does Etsy take from a sale?
A: In the US, Etsy takes 6.5% of the item price plus shipping, payment processing of 3% + USD 0.25, and USD 0.20 for the listing. On a USD 45 print with free shipping that is USD 4.73, about 11% of the sale. An Offsite Ads sale adds 12% or 15%.
Q: Does Etsy charge fees on shipping?
A: Yes. The 6.5% transaction fee, payment processing and the Offsite Ads fee are all charged on the shipping you charge as well as the item price, so free shipping built into the price costs the same in fees as a separate shipping charge.
Q: What is the Offsite Ads fee?
A: When a buyer clicks one of Etsy's ads on another website and buys within 30 days, Etsy charges 15% of the order total, or 12% if your shop made USD 10,000 or more in the past 365 days. It is never more than USD 100 for an order.
Q: Why does the calculator ask for an exchange rate?
A: Etsy states the listing fee (USD 0.20) and the Offsite Ads cap (USD 100) in US dollars. If your shop uses another currency, type how many units of your currency one US dollar costs today; the calculator never guesses a rate.
Q: How do I find my break-even price?
A: Enter your provider's product and shipping cost. The break-even price is the lowest item price that covers those costs and every Etsy fee on the sale, with your shipping charge unchanged. Price above it to make a profit.
Q: Is anything I type sent anywhere?
A: No. The calculator runs in your browser; nothing you type leaves your device.

## Etsy Listing Photo Checker: Size, Shape and Thumbnail Crop
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/etsy-photo-checker/
Free Etsy listing photo checker: see each image's pixel size, shape, file type and square thumbnail crop against Etsy's own photo guidance. Nothing is uploaded.

Short answer: Etsy recommends listing photos at least 2000 pixels wide and tall, a horizontal (landscape) or square first photo, and a .jpg, .gif, .png, .svg or .heic file. Keep the artwork away from the edges so a square thumbnail crop keeps it whole. Choose your images below to check them in your browser.

Q: What size should Etsy listing photos be?
A: Etsy's help article recommends listing photos with a width and height of at least 2000 pixels, so buyers can zoom in. It also says the first photo should be at least 635 pixels wide and tall to avoid showing up lower in searches.
Q: What shape should the first Etsy photo be?
A: Etsy asks for a horizontal (landscape) or square first photo. Vertical photos are fine later in the listing, but as a first photo they lose more of the picture when thumbnails are cropped.
Q: Why does my Etsy thumbnail cut off the art?
A: Thumbnails are cropped, and Etsy advises leaving enough border that an image can be cropped to square. Keep the artwork inside the dashed square the checker draws, away from the edges of a landscape photo.
Q: Is there a file size limit for Etsy photos?
A: Etsy's image help article notes that images larger than 1 MB may not finish uploading, especially on a slower connection. The checker flags files over 1 MB as worth knowing, not as a failure: a sharp 4096 px export is often larger and uploads fine on a good connection.
Q: Which file types does Etsy accept?
A: Etsy's help article lists .jpg, .gif, .png, .svg and .heic. Save WebP, TIFF or AVIF files as JPEG or PNG before you upload them.
Q: Are my photos uploaded?
A: No. The checker reads each image's size and type in your browser and draws the preview on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere.

## Frame and Mat Size Calculator: Mat Opening and Frame Size
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/frame-mat-calculator/
Free frame and mat size calculator: enter a print size and mat border to get the mat opening, the frame size to order and the nearest ready-made frame. Inches or cm.

Short answer: cut the mat opening about 1/8 inch (3 mm) smaller than the print on each edge, then add the border on every side. An 8 × 10 print with 1.5 inch borders needs a 10.75 × 12.75 inch frame, or fits a standard 11 × 14 frame with borders of about 1.6 and 2.1 inches. Enter your print below.

Q: How much smaller should a mat opening be than the print?
A: About 1/8 inch (3 mm) on each edge, so the mat holds the print: 1/4 inch (6 mm) less in each direction overall. An 8 × 10 inch print gets a 7.75 × 9.75 inch opening.
Q: What size frame do I need for an 8 × 10 print with a mat?
A: With 1.5 inch borders the mat and frame rebate are 10.75 × 12.75 inches, so a custom frame is that size. The nearest ready-made frame is 11 × 14 inches, which gives about 1.625 inch borders at the sides and 2.125 inches top and bottom.
Q: What is bottom weighting?
A: Making the bottom border slightly wider than the top and sides, a traditional framing touch that stops the art looking as if it is sliding down. The calculator offers a bottom border a quarter wider or half as wide again.
Q: What is the rebate size of a frame?
A: The inside size of the frame's lip: the size of the glass, mat and backing it holds. Order a custom frame by its rebate size; the outside is bigger by the width of the frame face on each side.
Q: Can I frame a print without a mat?
A: Yes. Enter a border of 0: the frame's rebate is then the print size itself, and the calculator tells you whether that is a ready-made frame size.

## Standard Frame Sizes Chart: US, Metric, A Sizes and Posters
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/frame-size-chart/
Standard frame sizes in inches and cm, A sizes and poster sizes, with each size's ratio and the print a matted frame usually holds. Find a frame for your print.

Short answer: common ready-made frames include 5 × 7, 8 × 10, 11 × 14, 16 × 20, 18 × 24 and 24 × 36 inches, and 13 × 18, 30 × 40, 50 × 70 cm and the A sizes. A matted frame usually holds the next size down, such as an 8 × 10 print in an 11 × 14 frame. Enter your print below to find frames that fit.

Q: What are the standard frame sizes?
A: In the US and Canada, common ready-made frames include 5 × 7, 8 × 10, 11 × 14, 12 × 16, 16 × 20, 18 × 24 and 24 × 36 inches. In the UK, Europe, Australia and India they include 13 × 18, 30 × 40, 40 × 50, 50 × 70 and 70 × 100 cm plus the A sizes. The chart lists each with its ratio.
Q: What size print goes in an 11 × 14 frame with a mat?
A: Usually an 8 × 10 inch print. With the mat overlapping the print by about 1/8 inch, that leaves borders of about 1.6 inches at the sides and 2.1 inches top and bottom.
Q: Is 11 × 17 a 2:3 size?
A: No. 11 × 17 is 1:1.55, so a 2:3 file printed at 11 × 17 loses about 3% to cropping. 12 × 18 is the 2:3 size nearby.
Q: What size is A3 in inches?
A: A3 is 29.7 × 42 cm, about 11.7 × 16.5 inches. Every A size has the same 1:1.414 ratio, so one file prints at all of them without cropping.
Q: Is 70 × 100 cm the same shape as A sizes?
A: Nearly but not quite: 70 × 100 is 7:10 (1:1.43) and A sizes are 1:1.414, about 1% apart. A file made for A sizes loses a sliver when printed at 70 × 100.

## Gallery Wall Layout Planner with Sizes and Hang Heights
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/gallery-wall-layout-planner/
Free gallery wall layout planner: enter frame sizes, gaps and your sofa width to get each frame's position, nail height and a to-scale diagram. Inches or cm.

Short answer: treat the gallery wall as one picture. Keep equal gaps of 3 to 6 inches (8 to 15 cm), make the group about two-thirds the width of the furniture below it, and centre it about 57 inches (145 cm) above the floor. Enter your frame sizes below to get each frame's position, its nail height and a diagram drawn to scale.

Q: How high should a gallery wall be hung?
A: A common guideline is to put the centre of the whole group about 57 inches (145 cm) above the floor, the eye-level line many galleries use. Over a sofa or sideboard, keep the bottom frames 6 to 10 inches (15 to 25 cm) above the furniture, ideally about 8 inches (20 cm), even if that moves the centre a little. The planner warns you if the gap is too small, too large or the frames overlap the furniture.
Q: How wide should a gallery wall be over a sofa?
A: About two-thirds of the sofa's width is the usual guideline, and up to three-quarters still looks planned. Over an 84 inch sofa that is roughly 56 to 63 inches for the whole group, frames and gaps included.
Q: How do I work out the nail height for each frame?
A: Take the frame's top-edge height from the table and subtract the drop: the distance from the top of the frame down to the taut wire or hook on the back. Enter that drop in the planner and it gives the hook height for every frame.
Q: Can I plan in centimetres?
A: Yes. Switch the unit to cm and the planner converts what you typed. The default 57 inch centre becomes 145 cm and the default 3 inch gap becomes 8 cm; other values are converted exactly.

## Gallery Wall Spacing Calculator: Gaps, Nail Spots, Heights
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/gallery-wall-spacing/
Free gallery wall spacing calculator for pairs, trios, rows and grids: even gaps, the total width, each nail's position and hook height above a sofa or bed. Inches or cm.

Short answer: hang gallery wall frames about 3 to 6 inches (8 to 15 cm) apart with equal gaps, and treat the group as one piece about two-thirds the width of the furniture below. For frames of the same width, the nails are one frame width plus one gap apart. Enter your frames below for every nail position and hook height.

Q: How far apart should pictures be hung in a gallery wall?
A: About 3 to 6 inches (8 to 15 cm) between frames is a common guideline, with every gap the same. Smaller frames sit well at the low end, large ones at the high end. Wider gaps make the pieces read as separate; narrower ones look cramped.
Q: How do I space three pictures over a sofa?
A: Treat the three as one piece about two-thirds the width of the sofa. Over an 84 inch sofa, three 16 × 20 inch frames with 3 inch gaps make a 54 inch group. Their nails are 19 inches apart. With a 34 inch sofa back and the bottom of the frames 8 inches above it, the tops of the frames are 62 inches from the floor; each nail goes that high minus the frame's hook drop.
Q: How far apart are the nails for frames of the same size?
A: One frame width plus one gap, measured centre to centre, for frames hung from a single central wire or hook. Three 16 inch frames with 3 inch gaps have nails 19 inches apart. For frames with two hooks each, measure the hook positions on each frame and offset them from its centre.
Q: Should the gaps be the same between rows?
A: Yes. In a grid, use the same gap vertically as horizontally so the group reads as one block. The calculator gives the row-to-row spacing for each grid.
Q: What if the group is wider than the sofa?
A: Use smaller frames, fewer frames or a smaller gap. The calculator says so plainly and measures every position from the centre line instead of the sofa's end.

## Triptych Split Calculator: Panorama to 2 or 3 Panels
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/panorama-triptych-split/
Free triptych split calculator: split a panorama into 2 or 3 panels with gaps, get each panel's size and position, and cut your image into panels in the browser.

Short answer: enter the artwork's width and height, 2 or 3 panels and the gap. Split evenly to keep the whole image (a 60 × 20 in panorama becomes three 20 × 20 in panels, 64 in wide with 2 in gaps), or keep the wall width and cut the gaps out so lines stay straight. Get each panel's size and position, and optionally cut your image into the panels in one ZIP.

Q: How do I split a panorama into a triptych?
A: Choose 3 panels and a gap. Split evenly to keep the whole image: a 60 × 20 in panorama becomes three 20 × 20 in panels and, with 2 in gaps, is 64 in wide on the wall. Or keep the wall width and cut out the gaps, so lines in the scene stay straight across them.
Q: What gap should a triptych have?
A: 2 to 3 inches (5 to 8 cm) between panels is common for living rooms; smaller gaps read as one piece, larger ones as three. Keep every gap the same.
Q: Which split mode should I use?
A: Split evenly when no part of the art may be lost, such as text or a centred subject. Cut out the gaps for landscapes and horizons, where the scene should look continuous behind the gaps.
Q: Is my image uploaded?
A: No. The image is cut into panels in your browser and downloaded as one ZIP; nothing is sent anywhere.

## Print Resolution Checker: How Big Can My Art Print?
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/print-resolution-checker/
Free print resolution checker for wall art sellers: your file's DPI at every common size, 5×7 to 24×36 and A5 to A1, and how much each crops. Nothing uploaded.

Short answer: divide your file's pixels by the print size in inches to get DPI. Aim for 300 DPI for fine-art prints; 7,200 × 10,800 pixels prints 24 × 36 in at 300 DPI. Choose a file below to check every common size at once.

Q: What resolution do I need to print 24 × 36 inches?
A: 7,200 × 10,800 pixels for 300 DPI. Large posters seen from a distance often look fine at 150–200 DPI, which is 3,600 × 5,400 to 4,800 × 7,200 pixels.
Q: What DPI should art prints be?
A: 300 DPI is the usual target for fine-art prints viewed up close. 200 DPI is often fine for medium prints, and 150 DPI for large posters seen from across a room.
Q: How do I find my file's pixel size?
A: Choose your file in the checker above; it reads the width and height in your browser. You can also type the numbers in.
Q: Why does my art crop on some sizes?
A: Every print size has a shape. A 2:3 file fits 8 × 12, 12 × 18 and 24 × 36 exactly, but an 8 × 10 print is 4:5, so part of a 2:3 file is cut off.
Q: Is my file uploaded?
A: No. The checker reads only the image's size in your browser. The file never leaves your device.

## Print Size Calculator: Which Print Sizes Fit My Art?
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/print-size-calculator/
Free print size calculator: enter your artwork's pixel size to find its ratio and every standard print size it fits without cropping, with the DPI of each. Inches and cm.

Short answer: divide the long side of your file by the short side to get its ratio; every print size in that ratio family prints without cropping. A 4800 × 7200 px file is 2:3, so it fits 8 × 12, 16 × 24 and 24 × 36 inches, sharp at 300 DPI up to 16 × 24. Enter your file's size below to see every size and its DPI.

Q: What print sizes can I make from a 2:3 file?
A: Every 2:3 size prints without cropping: 4 × 6, 8 × 12, 12 × 18, 16 × 24, 20 × 30, 24 × 36 and 40 × 60 inches, and 20 × 30, 40 × 60, 60 × 90 and 100 × 150 cm. How large you can go depends on the pixels: at 300 DPI, a 4800 × 7200 px file reaches 16 × 24 inches.
Q: Which sizes fit a 4:5 file?
A: 8 × 10, 16 × 20, 24 × 30 and 32 × 40 inches, and 24 × 30, 40 × 50 and 80 × 100 cm. 11 × 14 is close but not the same shape (11:14), so a 4:5 file loses about 2% to cropping there.
Q: Is 70 × 100 cm the same ratio as A sizes?
A: No. 70 × 100 cm is 7:10 (1:1.43); A sizes are 1:1.414. They are about 1% apart, so a file made for one crops slightly at the other. The calculator keeps them as separate families.
Q: What sizes fit a 3:1 panorama?
A: 12 × 36, 14 × 42, 16 × 48, 20 × 60 and 24 × 72 inches, or 30 × 90 and 50 × 150 cm, hung wide. A 9000 × 3000 px panorama prints 30 × 10 inches at 300 DPI and 60 × 20 inches at 150 DPI.
Q: How many pixels do I need for a 24 × 36 print?
A: 7,200 × 10,800 pixels for 300 DPI. Large prints seen from across a room are often printed at 150 to 200 DPI, which is 3,600 × 5,400 to 4,800 × 7,200 pixels.

## Print Size Converter: Inches, cm and Pixels at Any DPI
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/print-size-converter/
Free print size converter: inches to cm, cm to inches and either to pixels at 72 to 300 DPI, with a table of common print sizes and A sizes in pixels.

Short answer: enter a width and a height in inches, centimetres or pixels and choose a DPI. The converter shows the size in all three units: 8 × 10 in is 20.3 × 25.4 cm and 2400 × 3000 px at 300 DPI. Below it, a table lists common print sizes and A sizes in centimetres, pixels and megapixels at that DPI.

Q: How many pixels is 8 × 10 at 300 DPI?
A: 2400 × 3000 px. Multiply each side in inches by the DPI: 8 × 300 and 10 × 300.
Q: How do I convert inches to centimetres?
A: Multiply by 2.54: 24 × 36 in is 61 × 91.4 cm. To go from centimetres to inches, divide by 2.54.
Q: What DPI should a print be?
A: 300 DPI is the usual target for prints seen up close. Large prints seen from further away often look fine at 150 to 200 DPI; check yours with the print resolution checker.
Q: How many pixels is A4 at 300 DPI?
A: 2480 × 3508 px (21 × 29.7 cm).

## Printable Wall Art Size Pack Maker: 5 Ratios, One ZIP
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/printable-size-pack/
Free printable wall art size pack maker: one file becomes full-resolution crops at 2:3, 3:4, 4:5, 11:14 and ISO A, in one ZIP. Made in your browser; nothing uploaded.

Short answer: choose one artwork file and the tool makes the largest crop at each of the five standard printable ratios, 2:3, 3:4, 4:5, 11:14 and ISO A, at full resolution, and downloads them in one ZIP. A slider moves the crops to keep the part of the art you want. A 4000 × 6000 px file gives a 4000 × 5000 px 4:5 crop. Nothing is uploaded.

Q: Which ratios should a printable wall art pack include?
A: Five ratios cover almost every standard frame: 2:3 (4 × 6 to 24 × 36), 3:4 (6 × 8 to 18 × 24), 4:5 (8 × 10, 16 × 20), 11:14 and ISO A (A5 to A1). Buyers print the size they need from the file of the right shape.
Q: Is the pack made at full resolution?
A: Yes. Each crop keeps the original pixels of the area it covers; nothing is resized or enlarged. PNG is lossless; JPEG at quality 95 makes smaller files.
Q: Can I choose what each crop keeps?
A: Yes. The slider moves every crop along the side that is cropped, from one edge (0%) through the centre (50%) to the other (100%). Check the previews before you download.
Q: Is my artwork uploaded?
A: No. The file is opened, cropped and zipped in your browser; nothing leaves your device.
Q: How large a file can it handle?
A: Files up to about 40 megapixels work on most computers. Phones limit how large an image the browser can make, so very large packs may fail there; use a computer for those.

## Wall Art Size Comparison Chart Maker: Free, To Scale
URL: https://wallmock.com/tools/wall-art-size-comparison-chart/
Free wall art size comparison chart maker: draw the sizes you sell to one true scale over a sofa, bed or console, in inches or cm, and download a PNG for your listing.

Short answer: enter the art sizes you sell, such as 12 × 18, 24 × 36 and 40 × 60 in, and choose a piece of furniture. The chart draws every size to one true scale above it, marks how much of the furniture's width each covers, and saves a PNG for your listing. It is a diagram, not a room photo, and furniture sizes are typical.

Q: How do I make a wall art size chart for Etsy?
A: Enter the sizes you sell, pick a piece of furniture, and download the PNG. Every size is drawn to the same scale, so buyers can compare them at a glance. Add it as one of your listing photos, next to your room mockups.
Q: Is the chart drawn to scale?
A: Yes: every artwork and the furniture share one scale. It is a diagram, though, not a photo of a room, and the image says so. Furniture sizes are typical retail sizes, so a buyer's own sofa or bed may differ.
Q: What size art goes over an 84 inch sofa?
A: Art about two-thirds to three-quarters of the sofa's width, 56 to 63 inches across, looks balanced; the chart marks each size against that guide. A 40 × 60 in landscape covers 71%.
Q: Does it work in centimetres?
A: Yes. Switch the unit to cm; the chart labels each size in both units, and ISO sizes such as A3 and A2 are named.
Q: Is my data uploaded?
A: No. The chart is drawn and saved in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere.
